newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RTZ-CRA says remains committed to Lihir.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RTZ-CRA says remains committed to Lihir.

text.p: Global mining group RTZ-CRA said on Wednesday it remained committed to its investment in the Lihir gold project in Papua New Guinea and continued to await a political solution to the Bougainville crisis.
RTZ-CRA chief executive Leon Davis made the comment when asked by reporters if the group had changed its mind on its PNG investments after this week's political crisis.
"You know we are in there with Lihir of course, which is a good investment I think," Davis said.

"We of course have not been in Bougainville for eight years. It's still a very valuable investment for us and we would like to go back, but we have always said we need to have a political settlement to ensure everybody wants us back."
RTZ-CRA owns 53.6 percent of mine operator Bougainville Copper Ltd, but the mine itself has been closed since mid 1989 because of secessionist unrest on the island.
The Papua New Guinea government's recent decision to hire mercenaries to help quell the Bougainville uprising is at the centre of this week's political crisis in the country.

On Monday, defence force commander Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok was dismissed after calling on Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan to resign over the mercenaries affair. Singirok has vowed to continue his political battle with the government.
